correctness.rationale: For fixed a=r−1 and c, the probability of a degree-j line is asymptotic to e^{−c}(log N)^{j−a}/(N j!). Thus smaller degrees disappear and, by independent lines on each separate side, degree r appears on each side with high probability. For the mixed factorial moments, conditioning on the crossings of s fixed rows and t fixed columns leaves disjoint sites. A crossing pattern with h>0 occupied cells costs O(p^h) relative to an empty pattern; losing v entries from any line's residual degree target costs O((log N)^{−v}) or makes that event impossible. The total loss exponent over the lines is 2h. This proves the stated independent Poisson limit, including a=0 where nonempty crossing patterns are impossible. Conditional on a specific cell being occupied, its two residual counts are independent and each has probability O(log N/N) of being at most r; the expected number of such doubly low occupied cells is O((log N)^3/N). On their absence, if the respective minimum degrees are at least r and r−1, all unoccupied cells meet the odd bound, and any occupied violation would force both endpoint degrees at most r+1. If both minima are at least r, the analogous calculation yields the even bound. Conversely the two degree-(r−1) lines intersect to disprove odd domination, and any degree-(r−1) line intersects a degree-r line on the other side to disprove even domination. Therefore the limit has the stated OR/AND and joint mass vector, with gap 2z(1−z), z=e^{−lambda}, maximized at z=1/2. Uniform-permutation coupling at c±epsilon sandwiches monotone success, and continuity gives the fixed-budget and hitting-time limits. If the fixed-budget assertion is read to include the Poisson counts and high-probability reduction as well, the same estimates apply directly: on M=O(N) prescribed sites in finitely many lines with h=O(1) prescribed hits, the fixed-budget probability of the pattern is (m)_h/(N²)_h times the product over i=0,…,M−h−1 of [1−(m−h)/(N²−h−i)], uniformly asymptotic to p^h(1−p)^{M−h} at p=m/N². This gives the same mixed moments, rarity bounds and first/second moments for degree r. The proof requires fixed r. Separately the bitboard replay /workspace/evidence/2.py exhausts all subsets of orders 2,3,4 and checks the open-neighbor identity and both deterministic implications wherever the high-probability hypotheses hold. /workspace/evidence/2.out gives counts; these finite checks do not establish the limiting laws.

value.rationale: A single critical window conceals two different reliability mechanisms despite the consecutive requirements: one needs a clean side, the other two. Resolving those events jointly, with a nonvanishing worst gap of one half, answers a natural random-placement question missed by deterministic minimum-cardinality theory. The occupied-edge estimate says precisely when it is valid to replace open-neighbor constraints by low-line statistics, and fixed-budget and hitting-time forms are mathematically useful. The result is not credited for the routine transfer alone and does not purport to be uniform in r.
